allowed_dependency_manifest.content: Fix an integer n greater than 1. Let f_n(x) = floor(n times x) minus the sum for integer k from 1 to n of floor(k times x) divided by k. Consider f_n as a function on all real numbers x. Determine all real x values at which f_n(x) is globally maximal, and determine the corresponding maximal value M(n) = max over real x of f_n(x).

payload.statement_nl: Let f : ℤ → ℝ → ℝ and g : ℤ → ℤ → ℝ be fixed families of real-valued functions. For every integer n with n > 1, every integer k with 0 ≤ k ≤ n - 1, and every real number t with k ≤ n*t < k + 1, one has f(n)(t) ≤ g(n)(k).

result_payload.candidate_counterexample: Take f(n)(t)=1 for all integers n and all real t, and g(n)(k)=0 for all integers n and k. Then for any n>1, any k with 0<=k<=n-1, and any t with k<=n*t<k+1, we have f(n)(t)=1>0=g(n)(k), contradicting the claim.
result_payload.proof_summary: The statement is not provable as written because no relation between the families f and g is assumed. A counterexample is given by constant families f(n)(t)=1 and g(n)(k)=0, for which the claimed inequality fails.

suspected_gaps: The lemma statement is too abstract and lacks any hypothesis linking f and g.
Under the literal reading, the universal inequality is false.

result_payload.stuck_point: No assumptions relate f(n)(t) and g(n)(k), so the universal inequality cannot be deduced.
